hero.filename: C-74 Globemaster unloading flour at Berlin Gatow during Operation Vittles.jpg
hero.title: File:C-74 Globemaster unloading flour at Berlin Gatow during Operation Vittles.jpg
hero.source: C-74 Globemaster unloading flour at Berlin Gatow during Operation Vittles
hero.description: A U. S. Air Force C-74 Globemaster plane touched down at Gatow airfield located in southwestern Berlin, Germany on Tuesday with more than 20 tons of flour from the United States. “Operation Vittles” otherwise known as the Berlin Airlift (June 24, 1948-May 12, 1949) was a combined effort of the western allies against the Soviet Union’s blockade of all land routes into Berlin. The German children look on as the flour bags are lowered on August 19, 1948.  Photo courtesy of National Archives and Records Administration.

gallery.filename: Sunderland 201 Sqn on Havel during Berlin Airlift 1948.jpg
gallery.title: File:Sunderland 201 Sqn on Havel during Berlin Airlift 1948.jpg
gallery.credit: This photograph MH 30687 comes from the collections of the Imperial War Museums.
gallery.source: Sunderland 201 Sqn on Havel during Berlin Airlift 1948
gallery.description: A Short Sunderland GR Mark 5 of No 201 Squadron, Royal Air Force, moored on the Havel in Berlin, Germany. The river Havel and lake Wannsee were used by Coastal Command Sunderlands from July until mid-December 1948, when the threat of winter ice suspended further use. The photograph shows members of the crew relaxing on the roof of their aircraft whilst their freight is unloaded.

gallery.filename: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-S85096, Berlin, Beseitigung von Grenz-Strassensperren.jpg
gallery.title: File:Bundesarchiv Bild 183-S85096, Berlin, Beseitigung von Grenz-Strassensperren.jpg
gallery.description:
For documentary purposes the German Federal Archive often retained the original image captions, which may be erroneous, biased, obsolete or politically extreme. Zentralbild/Rudolph
Berlin im Mai 1949
Um eine Störung des Wirtschaftslebens in der sowjetischen Besatzungszone und in Berlin zu verhindern, sperrt die sowjetische Besatzungsmacht den Personen- und Güterverkehr zwischen Westdeutschland und Berlin am 24. Juni 1948. Diese Beschränkungen werden nach Verhandlungen von Regierungsvertretern der vier Siegermächte am 12. Mai 1949 aufgehoben.

UBz: Am 11. Mai werden die Strassensperren an den Übergangsstellen vom sowjetischen in die Westsektoren, hier Jakob- Ecke Seydelstrasse, beseitigt.
categories: Images from the German Federal Archive
Women at work in the German Democratic Republic
